## Summary

Settled all three of the scenario-4 pre-registration's open items on run-owner rulings and wrote them into PRE-REGISTRATION.md as D24, D25 and D26. Every one tightened the design, so D3 holds. Measured the operating characteristics of the temptation floor rather than assuming them: the old k=4 / 2-of-4 gate admits a p=0.25 constraint 26.2% of the time, which under a 40% weak-authoring bias makes 16.0% of the admitted set weak, so the gate went to k=6 / 4-of-6 (3.3%). Three findings changed the shape of the items themselves. The per-constraint concentration cap never binds at 45-60 constraints (2.0% of the denominator), so the third item named the wrong control and a 40% per-repo cap with a 3-repo minimum was added to fill the real gap. The rule field cannot be phrasing-matched to the 471 eligible decisions: only 62 usable ruled decisions exist and they come from just brillo and sofar, while sofar-cloud and algrowth have never carried a standing constraint, so rule-voice fidelity there is borrowed and disclosed. The lone-planted-rule worry is dead, since 10 of 21 rule-carrying initiatives hold exactly one. The temptation floor turns out never to have been run for any trap, the 5 anchor constraints included, so tightening the gate costs nothing retroactively and the anchor comparison stays clean. Plan rebuilt around the rulings, with 4.4 added for the discrimination test and 5.1 gaining the unmeasured sofar per-session cost.
